name: PerpPair same-actor virtual PnL realization
summary: PerpPair let one economic actor provide leveraged virtual liquidity, trade against that same virtual reserve state, and immediately realize the resulting LP PnL as withdrawable Vault collateral. addLiquidity records the LP's virtual balances and debts, trade moves the shared virtual curve, calcPnL marks the actor's combined LP and trader positions against that moved state, and realizePnL credits the positive result to real collateral without an independent realization price, delay, or separation between the LP and trader. The violated invariant is that a participant must not be able to turn a self-created virtual counterparty loss into a claim on scarce vault collateral.

loss.notes: The Vault receives exactly 30,000 + 15,000 + 10,000 + 5,000 = 60,000 USDC and sends 183,283.399597 + 42,364.335584 = 225,647.735181 USDC in the sole successful loss receipt, for gross depletion of 165,647.735181 USDC. Its archive USDC balance falls from 165,647.735882 to 0.000701, exactly the same net change, so no unrelated same-block adjustment is required. The 60,000 USDC is genuine collateral consideration retained by the victim. The external financing source receives 60,030 USDC after supplying 60,000, leaving 165,617.735181 USDC as attacker proceeds; the 30-USDC financing premium explains why proceeds are lower than gross victim loss and is not subtracted again. Later approval and bridge deposits move all proceeds downstream, do not touch the Vault, and are excluded from the exploit-time boundary.

ageReset.description: PerpPair is a direct contract. Its runtime is absent one block before creation and byte-identical at creation and immediately before the incident. No proxy or module activation exists, and later parameter changes do not introduce the same-actor virtual-PnL realization path.

sources.note: Reviewed the incident receipt and call trace, every USDC transfer touching the Vault, financing source, attacker and helpers, archive balances at blocks 30,067,820 and 30,067,821, attacker nonce scope, PerpPair's verified runtime and parameter history, and the canonical creation receipt. Source-3 creates top-level helper 0xb87275489272ce1c4be358fc5856ea3273093cf8 at attacker nonce 0. Nonce 1 repeats its call and reverts; nonce 2 is source-1 and creates two LP/trader helper pairs that execute addLiquidity, trade and realizePnL on PerpPair. The Vault receives 60,000.000000 USDC and sends 225,647.735181; its archive balance falls by exactly 165,647.735181. The financing source supplies 60,000 and receives 60,030, while 165,617.735181 reaches the EOA. The top-level helper has zero USDC before and after the loss; the EOA goes from zero to 165,617.735181, then nonces 3 through 19 approve and deposit exactly that amount into a bridge, leaving both at zero without a return to the Vault. PerpPair was top-level created in source-2 at block 29,416,825 index 0, timestamp 1,772,548,244. Its 24,427-byte runtime is absent one block earlier and hashes to 0x7469f2e9ada0b1f20a8b8a7a2a99f13e9e9812eb49b3ac38e1d26f75ee1cdacd at creation and immediately before the incident; EIP-1967 implementation and beacon slots are zero. From creation through incident-minus-one, the contract emits no LockedParameterUpdate. Its three ParametersUpdated events round-trip the oracle and, in source-4, reduce only the frontend fee share from 300,000 to 50,000. Fee, funding, leverage, and the direct addLiquidity/trade/calcPnL/realizePnL composition remain unchanged, so those configuration events do not reset the causal code age.
